# Radio group

## When to use it

**In Multi-brand:** Picks a plan.

- **Use it when:** Two to about five options where the answer is one of them.
- **Not when:** Many options (select), many answers (checkboxes), or a setting that applies at once (switch).

Instead:

- [Checkbox](./checkbox.md): More than one may be true.
- [Select](./select.md): The list is long.

## Words

- Shared structure: object, state, next step.
- Brand tone lives in headlines and marketing copy, not in errors.
- Errors and confirmations read the same in every brand.
- Use: Get started, Plan, Order. Avoid: Brand-specific words in errors, Jargon.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Get started

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

| Keyboard | What happens | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| undefined | Arrow keys move the choice; Tab leaves the group. | undefined |

Test before you ship:

- [ ] The options are a group with a question as its name. undefined

## Look closer

<div class="odv-anat-link"><a href="./radio-group-anatomy">Anatomy reference →</a><span>Each part of Radio group, and how the design decisions reach it: the answer, the rule, the token and the value you see.</span></div>

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add radio-group
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Radio group reads 14 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Radio group's tokens to change Radio group alone.
